summary.text: A previously healthy 42-year-old man was admitted with generalized muscle pain, dry skin and mild facial puffiness of eight days duration with a choking sensation in the throat. He denied strenuous exercise, alcohol, trauma and recent medication use. Examination showed facial puffiness, dry skin, minimal non-pitting lower limb edema and a small goiter, without muscle wasting or weakness.

Laboratory testing showed very high creatine kinase and myoglobin, elevated thyroid antibody titers and mild creatinine elevation with acute kidney injury; urine was negative for myoglobinuria and hematuria. ECG, chest X-ray and laryngoscopy were normal and echocardiography showed a minimal pericardial effusion with ejection fraction 58%. A probable diagnosis of hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto's thyroiditis with rhabdomyolysis was made.

He received intravenous fluids and oral levothyroxine, his symptoms improved and CK and myoglobin decreased, and he was discharged on Day 4. On follow-up the muscle enzymes decreased further and renal parameters normalized, with complete symptom resolution and return to regular activities, so further workup for muscle disease was not carried out.
